description:
No spec subject (diagnostics enhancement; touches specled.tagged_tests realization when implemented).

Follow-up from specled_-odl. The 2026-07-26 cz0-session observation reported 'failing tests: test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255' where line 255 was blank on the tree that ran — the descriptor path (TaggedTests.Formatter -> JSONL artifact -> Attribution.descriptor/1) can only emit ExUnit declaration lines (test.tags.line), so the anomaly is unexplained: either the event carried wrong data or the compiled beam did not match the inspected source. specled_-odl hardened the timing side but could not diagnose this.

Two changes: (1) include the event id (module + test name) alongside file:line in failing-test and hang-suspect descriptors in SpecLedEx.TaggedTests.Attribution.descriptor/1, so the next mismatched line self-identifies regardless of line drift — this changes finding-message format asserted at e.g. test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:1519 ('timed out while running test/alpha_test.exs:42') and will show as realization drift on attribution.ex; (2) set SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR in orchestration/gate environments so a red tagged_tests leg preserves the inner suite's full output (the verifier's forensic capture already exists in preserve_failed_output/2 but was unset during every observation to date, which is why no failure output was ever captured).

comments.text: Scope addition from specled_-odl: test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:1452 ('attribution artifact names embed the OS pid and random entropy') remains an open flake site with no credible mechanism — no tight budget, no sleep, serial module. When implementing the forensic capture here, confirm it would preserve enough of the inner run's output to diagnose an assertion-level failure in that test (the report status, the artifact name actually produced, and the shim's stdout).

FINDING: the docs_identifier_lint_test.exs:255 line anomaly is explained — the reporting path is exonerated.

Evidence (git archaeology, 2026-07-26):
- Test files are .exs: ExUnit compiles them from disk at run time, no beam cache. An artifact event's line therefore always reflects the on-disk file AT RUN START, not any stale compile.
- The cz0 session's branch (specled_-cz0/spec-honesty, still alive) shows seven micro-commits touching this exact file. Across them, test 'a fabricated, unmarked finding code IS flagged' sat at lines 182, 231, 242, 250, 256, 266, 268 — the file churned +/-6 lines around 255 all session.
- 4c9aa6864 has that test at 250 and the 'evidence/*' test head at 256/257 with 255 blank — precisely the state the original comment describes inspecting. Adjacent states (833a83fe, 966464d9) have an @tag at 255 and a test decl at 256.
- Conclusion: the failing run executed an uncommitted working state where a test declaration sat at 255; the 'line 255 is blank' inspection read a different (shifted) state. 'No edits between runs' was wrong at file granularity — the session was editing this exact file between spec.check invocations.

Impact on this ticket's scope: the descriptor-id change is MORE valuable, not less — a test NAME is shift-proof where a line number is not; this failure mode (report generated against tree state A, investigated against tree state B) will recur in any session that edits between gate runs. Two scope additions worth making: (1) preserve the attribution artifact JSONL alongside the SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR capture on failure (run_merged_command's `after File.rm(artifact_path)` currently destroys it — it is primary evidence); (2) have the forensic capture record run-time provenance (git rev-parse HEAD + dirty-file list) so report-vs-inspection tree skew is detectable next time.

Still genuinely open: WHY a doc-integrity lint test failed once-in-five under load (the assertions near every candidate line are pure-constant), and the verifier_test.exs:1452 site. Both need the armed forensics; neither needs the reporting path investigated further.

Final-tier runs: 1

The four changes:
1. Attribution.descriptor/1 emits "file:line (Module.test name)". The event id is shift-proof where a line is not, so the tree-skew failure mode self-identifies. Degrades to whichever half an event carries.
2. preserve_failed_output/3 records run provenance: git_head plus git_dirty (path list bounded at 50, omitted count stated). Best-effort - git absent or a non-work-tree root records "unavailable" rather than costing the caller its log.
3. A failing/timed-out merged run copies its attribution JSONL to <capture-basename>.attribution.jsonl before run_merged_command's `after File.rm/1` destroys it. Same basename so log and artifact stay correlatable in a shared capture dir.
4. SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR armed at tmp/specled-command-output in every gate path this repo owns: .claude/settings.json (agent shells - the environment where every observation to date happened), `make check` (target-scoped export, so `make test` does not litter it), scripts/check_specs.sh (default when unset). CI keeps its runner-temp location.

Policy recorded as specled.decision.gate_failure_forensics (affects specled.verification + specled.tagged_tests); it is also what cleared branch_guard_missing_decision_update.

Confirmation asked for by the 2026-07-26T11:08:06Z comment (verifier_test.exs:1452, now :1470) - MEASURED, not reasoned. Forced each assertion red in turn:
- artifact-name assertion: already prints the name actually produced ("specled_attr_12921_e2fa95536f13.jsonl"). Diagnosable as-is.
- status assertion: printed only `"fail" == "pass"`. No finding, no exit code, no inner command - preserving that verbatim preserves nothing. GAP, fixed in 098dbba4: the assertion now carries report["findings"], and the same forced failure names exit_code=7, the exact merged command, and both subjects' finding messages.
- the shim's stdout for that test is the attr_path.txt content, which the name assertion already surfaces.

Scope note (disclosed, not silent): giving specled_-n5s's write-path exception contract an owning clause in specled.coverage_capture resolves specled_-npo as a byproduct. See the comment on npo.

Deferred must requirements: none.

  - specled.verify.command_capture_run_provenance: PARTIALLY covered by

- Intent-level scope concerns: none. mix.exs and mix.lock untouched (0 files);

  - `mix test test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs:{1470,1520,1957,1995,2042,2080}`

  - `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` clean after reverting my experiments.
- Corpus-scoped claims (doc-shaped diffs, per step 7.5): 9 claims validated, 7

  Executed:

Verdict: FAIL

Gaps:
- specled.tagged_tests.failed_run_preserves_attribution_artifact: the
  best-effort clause is untested. The requirement states in its own text that a
  filesystem failure "shall not alter the verification result, and shall emit a
  one-line stderr warning rather than failing silently" — the sibling
  requirement specled.verify.command_output_capture_dir has exactly such a test
  (verifier_test.exs:2080 asserts `stderr =~ "specled: forensic output capture
  failed"` under an unwritable dir); the new one has none. MUTATION-PROVEN: I
  deleted the entire `rescue e in File.Error` block from
  preserve_failed_artifact/2 (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2216-2224) and the
  suite stayed green — 78 tests, 0 failures across verifier_test.exs +
  tagged_tests/. Failure mode not caught: with the rescue gone, an unwritable
  `<capture>.attribution.jsonl` target raises File.Error out of
  run_merged_command/5 and crashes the verification run — the precise outcome
  the requirement forbids, on the loaded/full-disk runners where the capture is
  most likely to fail and most needed.
- specled.verify.command_capture_run_provenance: the truncation clause is
  untested. The requirement states the dirty list shall be truncated "after a
  fixed bound" with "the omitted count stated"; the only test (:1995) creates
  ONE dirty file, so it never reaches @provenance_dirty_limit (50).
  MUTATION-PROVEN: I replaced `Enum.split(entries, @provenance_dirty_limit)`
  with `{entries, []}` and dropped the `... and N more` suffix
  (lib/specled_ex/verifier.ex:2489-2491) — same run, 78 tests, 0 failures.
  Failure mode not caught: a mid-rebase or unignored-build-dir tree emits
  thousands of paths inline, which is the exact scenario the code comment says
  the bound exists for. `dirty_provenance(nil)` ("git_dirty: unavailable") and
  `dirty_provenance("")` ("git_dirty: none (clean work tree)") are likewise
  unreached by any test.
- Deliverable self-contradiction (Makefile:46-50 vs .claude/settings.json:2-4):
  the Makefile comment claims "Exported for `check` only, so an ordinary `make
  test` does not litter the directory with the suite's deliberate command
  failures." That is false in the very environment this same commit arms and
  that the ADR names as primary ("agent shells — the environment where every
  observation to date happened"): .claude/settings.json sets
  SPECLED_COMMAND_OUTPUT_DIR globally, so every `mix test` / `make test` in an
  agent shell inherits it. PROVEN BY EXECUTION: with the var set, running
  test/specled_ex/verifier_test.exs deposited 2 capture logs
  (specled_cmd_38249_9853ed0afdda.log, specled_cmd_38249_9e8658964b1b.log) from
  the suite's deliberate command failures. Behaviour is harmless (gitignored,
  0 test failures) — the defect is that the shipped rationale states an outcome
  the shipped configuration negates. Fix is a comment correction or a
  settings.json narrowing, not a code change.

Notes (advisory only — none of these change the verdict):
- ADR imprecision: "Each capture costs two `git` invocations" is really "at most
  two" — outside a git work tree run_provenance/1 short-circuits after
  `rev-parse HEAD` and issues one. The ADR's own next sentence describes that
  branch, so this reads as loose wording rather than a false claim.
- .claude/settings.json uses a RELATIVE path ("tmp/specled-command-output")
  where the Makefile ($(CURDIR)/...) and check_specs.sh ($ROOT/...) both use
  absolute. File.mkdir_p!/1 resolves it against the OS process cwd, so an agent
  invoking `mix spec.check` from a subdirectory writes captures to
  <subdir>/tmp/specled-command-output, which the anchored `/tmp/` .gitignore
  rule does NOT cover. Worth an absolute-path follow-up ticket.
- Descriptors now embed parentheses and are joined with ", " into messages that
  themselves parenthesise the list — e.g. `tagged_tests cover failed: req.a
  (test/a.exs:9 (M.fail))` (verifier.ex:570-573). Cosmetic nesting; and a test
  name containing ", " was already ambiguous under the old id fallback, so this
  is not a regression.
- The ticket description predicted the descriptor change "will show as
  realization drift on attribution.ex". It did not, and .spec/realization_hashes.json
  is correctly absent from the diff: the bound realizations are
  SpecLedEx.TaggedTests.Attribution.attribute/2 and .read_artifact/1, and the
  edit lands in private helpers below them. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`
  reports no drift. Prediction wrong, deliverable correct.
- No mocks anywhere in the new tests: no Mox, no Mock* module, no injected
  behaviour. The seams used are real subprocesses (written shell shims as
  verification commands), real `git init`/commit at a FixtureCase tmp root, and
  System.put_env. That is the honest, high-fidelity end of the seam spectrum.
- The tree is exactly as committed: all four experiments (shim exit 7, bogus
  artifact regex, rescue deletion, truncation deletion) were reverted with
  `git checkout --` and `git status --short` is empty.
